This atlas therefore treats environment, method, date, document digest and limitations as part of the evidence, not administrative decoration. The measurements remain private experiment reports, but the public summaries preserve enough structure to explain why a conclusion was drawn and where a stronger conclusion would need new work.

articles.title: Nearby source is a reference, not the missing kernel
articles.description: Version identity, provenance and measured interfaces constrain what public source can tell us.
articles.body:
## Begin with the target's own identity

The inspected software identifies itself as iPhone OS 1.1.4, build 4A102. The kernel reports a 933-era ARM XNU build. That identity should remain fixed while comparing public source. Similar Darwin version strings or nearby desktop releases do not make another tree the source of this binary. [E01](/ios/evidence/E01/) [E27](/ios/evidence/E27/)

The source survey examined official distribution metadata, tags and relevant implementation directories. No matching public XNU 933 ARM implementation was found in that inspected set. The result is deliberately scoped: it is a survey of named repositories and revisions, not proof that no historical archive could exist anywhere.

## Three useful references with different roles

| Reference | What it can help explain | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nearby Apple desktop XNU | Common Mach, BSD and IOKit concepts and interface changes | The target ARM machine layer |
| Later community ARM XNU | Shape of ARM platform initialization and board code | 4A102 ABI or userspace compatibility |
| Contemporaneous family source | Class matching and subsystem design | Exact embedded method layout and calling convention |

The inspected darwin-on-arm tree contains relevant ARM platform material, but it is a later kernel family. Replacing the running target with it would create a new compatibility project, not automatically finish the current port.

Likewise, a source header can describe a newer overload than the one called by the embedded target. That is why the storage completion work measured the exact boundary and tested it with independent receivers. [E10](/ios/evidence/E10/)

## Symbols are aids, not recovered declarations

Names from a binary can make the investigation understandable. A decompiler can suggest object structure and control flow. Those tools still require checks against instruction bytes, call sites and runtime objects. An inferred signature may be wrong even when its name is correct.

The preservation record should distinguish a published source declaration, a binary observation, an inferred role and a tested interface. Merging those categories into an apparently authoritative reconstructed header makes later mistakes hard to locate.

## Reuse also has a provenance boundary

Public availability is not a single license. Apple source archives, Linux drivers, firmware projects and community experiments carry their own terms. This atlas links to those works and summarizes the concepts relevant to the research. Its MIT license covers the original publication material and website; it does not relicense the referenced source or Apple software.

The same distinction applies to upstream demonstrations. An author's successful emulator boot is an upstream report until independently reproduced under a recorded local configuration. The project's own reference reproduction has a separate evidence identity.

## A durable research practice

Pin the source revision, record what was inspected, identify the question it answered and state what remains unverified. A negative finding should include its search scope. An interface inference should have a path to a discriminating test.

This approach keeps source archaeology productive without allowing familiar code to substitute for the actual legacy system under study. It also makes the publication maintainable: a newly found source tree can extend or revise a specific survey result instead of forcing readers to reinterpret every earlier claim.

articles.title: Preserve the chain of evidence
articles.description: A research atlas should let a future reader distinguish the measurement from the story around it.
articles.body:
## Treat a claim as structured data

A useful preservation claim includes the software/build identity, execution environment, method, observation and limitation. Its identity changes when any of those changes. “Buttons work” is too broad; “three short physical Power taps produced three guest edge pairs and the observed setup/black/setup sequence” is inspectable. [E20](/ios/evidence/E20/)

This atlas stores evidence records separately from explanatory articles. Articles can connect several records without silently changing their scopes. The concept map and guided tours are generated from the same article relationships, while the evidence pages show where each reported result is used.

The organizational inspiration is Understand-Anything's linked knowledge and guided exploration. The publication adapts those ideas to concepts and claims rather than exposing a function-by-function graph of the implementation repository.

## Separate observation from interpretation

The missing BOOT_TIME experiment observed comparable later milestones with different console output. The interpretation that a logging-route race explains the difference is plausible, but the route was not directly traced. Both statements belong in the record, with different confidence. [E24](/ios/evidence/E24/)

The empty-framebuffer case similarly requires a correction history. The early probe output did not validate source content; the known-pattern and mapped-descriptor control changed the interpretation. Removing the old hypothesis entirely would lose the reason the improved measurement matters. [E16](/ios/evidence/E16/)

A useful correction entry follows: earlier belief, discriminating observation, replacement statement, remaining limit. “We were wrong” is less useful than naming exactly which inference exceeded the data.

## Make acceptance falsifiable

A clean storage gate can specify an unchanged root hash, a complete data copy, a read-only consistency check, no recorded request failures and observed recovery return. Those postconditions can fail independently. The two consecutive physical trials passed that stated gate, while leaving the unexercised overflow path and power-loss behavior open. [E13](/ios/evidence/E13/)

An acceptance marker should never be renamed to imply a larger milestone. A synthetic CPU or pixel test remains synthetic even when it is a necessary prerequisite for original-client work.

## Publish useful evidence without distributing the experiment

This repository contains original prose, diagrams, curated measurement summaries and document digests. It does not include the source implementation repository, raw firmware, images, binary modifications, private logs, device identifiers or session conversations.

That boundary imposes an honest limitation: the public package is not a complete reproducibility archive. A digest identifies the reviewed private document if an authorized reviewer later obtains it; the digest alone cannot independently verify its contents. Public primary references corroborate architecture and source context, while the local experiment summaries remain reported observations.

## Keep editions stable

The first edition has a fixed source revision and date. In-progress work after that boundary is not silently promoted into the published frontier. A later result should add a reviewed evidence record, revise affected articles and note which earlier conclusion it supersedes.

The original source survey is a good example: “not found in these inspected releases” can be updated if new material appears, without pretending the earlier scoped observation was universal. [E27](/ios/evidence/E27/)

Preservation succeeds when the next researcher inherits both the useful result and the information needed to question it. A polished presentation should make that discipline easier to follow, not smooth away the uncertainty.

evidence.title: One kernel, different products
evidence.method: Archive metadata and full-byte hash comparison
evidence.observation: The inspected iPhone and iPod touch 1.1.4/4A102 archives contain a byte-identical kernelcache. Their board trees, bootloaders and primary root images differ.
evidence.limits: Shared kernel identity does not establish cross-product userspace, peripheral or telephony compatibility.

evidence.limits: Both runs recorded zero overflow-path uses. These results do not validate queue saturation, arbitrary power loss or application-setting persistence.

evidence.limits: Earlier root mount labels did not prevent every metadata write path. The file experiment is QEMU evidence, not a physical application-setting result.

evidence.limits: This is a false positive about a detection predicate, not evidence of a working modem or a complete iPhone profile.

corrections.belief: A missing BOOT_TIME line means boot stalled.
corrections.test: Compare later service milestones and runtime-state files across matched physical runs.
corrections.result: The later milestones matched even when the console marker did not. A logging-route race is plausible but untraced.
corrections.replacement: Use independent progress and response evidence; keep QEMU runs that lacked later milestones unresolved.

corrections.belief: The submitted surfaces are zero, so a renderer is missing.
corrections.test: Present a known pattern and validate the descriptor read path before classifying the original source.
corrections.result: The early read route was ineffective. A mapped-descriptor capture subsequently showed original-client setup pixels.
corrections.replacement: Verify the observer and transfer length before drawing conclusions about the source. General GPU coverage remains open.

corrections.belief: The radio-present message establishes a modeled radio.
corrections.test: Compare the guest detection predicate with the model's actual register responses.
corrections.result: An unsupported input defaulted to zero, satisfying the presence predicate despite the absence of a radio model.
corrections.replacement: A log message proves a code path. It does not prove the hardware capability named by that path.

corrections.belief: A backed physical address rules out a translation problem.
corrections.test: Walk the active descriptors and inspect the fault class and interpretation controls.
corrections.result: The A53 access-flag interpretation rejected a legacy descriptor even though its physical target was backed RAM.
corrections.replacement: Translation, permissions and interpretation must agree before an access is valid.

corrections.belief: MACH Reboot means the device reset cleanly.
corrections.test: Observe return to recovery and check the complete post-run data image.
corrections.result: An earlier printed marker preceded an integration failure. Corrected trials independently established actual recovery return.
corrections.replacement: Require the state transition and its postconditions, not merely the log before it.

corrections.belief: A black screen is necessarily a display-driver failure.
corrections.test: Inspect selected surfaces and backing bytes, then trace the original client's blank request.
corrections.result: One QEMU transition was explicitly requested by SpringBoard's dimming path while prior pixels remained intact.
corrections.replacement: Separate intentional black, failed presentation, backlight policy and system liveness. Attribute each physical case with its own evidence.

corrections.belief: A quiet CPU and a recovery charging label settle the power question.
corrections.test: Measure the USB input state during XNU and compare battery readings over a controlled interval.
corrections.result: The accepted USB-controller state yielded usable input and net battery gain in the measured configuration.
corrections.replacement: Measure the energy path in the target state; idle residency and charging are independent observations.

glossary: The 32-bit execution state used by the native XNU research on the Cortex-A53. Application instruction support alone does not establish kernel compatibility.
Application binary interface: the concrete calling, layout and preservation rules that independently compiled components must agree on.
The Allwinner SoC used by the original PinePhone in this research. It is not the PinePhone Pro platform.
A producer encountering limited capacity in a downstream queue or sink. It needs an explicit admission and progress policy.
The runtime structure through which a loader supplies the kernel with memory and platform context.
A launchd log message used during research. Its absence from a console is insufficient evidence that userspace failed to progress.
The legacy shared graphics-surface service observed in this build. Source storage must be distinguished from active display scanout.
A memory policy in which a write to a shared mapping can require a private copy. Compatibility operations must preserve that behavior.
A structure describing a memory region or translation. In this atlas, a page-table descriptor and an IOKit memory descriptor are different objects.
Structured platform metadata. The Apple-format tree given to XNU is distinct from the native board FDT, and its live contents can differ from the archive.
Flattened device tree: a board-description format used in the native platform environment, separate from the inspected legacy Apple tree format.
A filesystem consistency check. A full-volume check is stronger than reading the clean-unmount bit, but does not prove arbitrary power-loss durability.
Generic Interrupt Controller: part of the native A64 interrupt-delivery path, with different semantics from the original Samsung platform's controllers.
A member of the HFS Plus filesystem family used by the inspected volumes. The native adapter retains the original kernel filesystem implementation.
Human Interface Device. The research follows the original event-service and client paths for button and touch delivery.
XNU's object, registry and driver-service framework. Construction, registration, matching and client operations are separate observable steps.
The original audio family required by the inspected media client. Publishing a compatible output does not establish sound playback.
The common original framebuffer interface retained around native presentation behavior in the display experiments.
Low-resolution analog-to-digital input used for the PinePhone volume-key ladder in the recorded button experiment.
The original iPhone product profile. Its 4A102 archive shares a kernelcache with N45AP while differing in board and root-image contents.
The original PowerVR graphics family associated with the Apple reference hardware. A setup-frame result does not certify general MBX command coverage.
Memory Management Unit: the translation and access-control machinery between a task's virtual address and a physical target.
The first-generation iPod touch profile used as the working original-device reference in this research.
A deliberately wrong or absent condition that should make a test reject the result. It checks whether the observer can detect the failure of interest.
Power-enable key events exposed by the PMIC. These supply the physical Power-button input in the accepted native experiment.
Power-management integrated circuit. Its target-state measurements help distinguish USB input availability, charging and peripheral power.
Selecting and making a frame available to the display path. It is distinct from rendering the source pixels and from device scanout timing.
The deliberately partial native-board model used to test selected A64 interfaces and original-client integrations.
The active pixel storage consumed by the display engine. Its lifetime and visibility are different from those of an application's source surface.
The original user-interface process studied through service startup, rendering, dimming and input response. A process being alive does not imply a complete UI session.
An obsolete ARM memory-exchange instruction observed in original userspace. Correct compatibility requires more than instruction decoding.
The units and counter used to represent time. A stale frequency declaration can change the real duration of delays and timeouts.
The display's vertical blank interval. A software notification or completed memory copy is not automatically evidence of physical VBlank synchronization.
Wait For Interrupt. Time spent waiting is evidence about CPU activity, not a complete measurement of board power or charging.
The kernel family underlying the target software. This research studies the measured 933-era ARM binary and native adaptations, not a recovered complete source tree.
